description: The quintessential 16th-note slap and pop groove emphasizing ghost notes and octave displacement.
focus: Slap and pop articulation

source.title: Slap It
source.author: Tony Oppenheim

title: Marcato en 4 — Acompañamiento en Negras (Botto Ej. 1)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Fundamental Tango Marcato en 4 from Mariano Botto (p. 14, Ej. 1). All 4 quarter notes are struck with downstroke marcato and choked immediately (staccato) using the right hand palm edge or left-hand fretboard release.
focus: Strict staccato chord choke on all 4 quarter-note beats in Am and E7
musicalRole: Orchestral guitar rhythmic motor, replicating the double-bass and bandoneón marcato

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Tango — Melodía de Tango Básico en Sol (Botto Ej. 2)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Classic tango melody from Mariano Botto (p. 16, Ej. 2). Demonstrates traditional Argentine phrasing: expressive upbeat pickups, syncopated quarter-notes, and chromatic resolutions moving from G Major to G minor.
focus: Expressive phrasing with rhythmic anticipation and traditional tango ornamentation
musicalRole: Lead voice for classical or electric tango guitar quartet

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Tango — Acompañamiento Sencillo de Tango Básico (Botto Ej. 3)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: First accompaniment arrangement for the basic tango melody (p. 18, Ej. 3). Demonstrates stable 4/4 marcato rhythm across G - D7 - C - E7 - Am - Gm progressions with clear root basses.
focus: Consistent root motion and rhythmic stability under the melody
musicalRole: Primary accompaniment guitar in traditional tango duo or trio

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Vals — Acompañamiento con Bajos Caminantes (Botto Ej. 4)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Second arrangement from Mariano Botto (p. 20, Ej. 4). Incorporates moving bass notes on the 4th beat to lead smoothly into the next chord, introducing inverted dominants (D7/A, E7/B).
focus: Walking bass notes on beat 4 with chordal marcato on beats 1, 2, and 3
musicalRole: Advanced rhythmic guitar comping with active counter-bass

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Tango — Acompañamiento con Acordes de Paso Cromáticos (Botto Ej. 5)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Third arrangement from Mariano Botto (p. 22, Ej. 5). Uses parallel chromatic passing chords (C7/G -> C#7/G#, Eb7/Bb -> D7/A) to inject tension and harmonic color into the tango groove.
focus: Rapid chromatic parallel chord sliding and accurate voice-leading in 4/4 marcato
musicalRole: Sophisticated harmonic accompaniment in modern and guardia nueva tango

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Marcato — Marcato 1–3 con Staccato (Botto Ej. 7)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Essential Argentine tango accompaniment from Mariano Botto (p. 24, Ej. 7). Beats 1 and 3 are struck with tremendous force and broad chord voicing, choked with dry staccato, while beats 2 and 4 are softer, playing only high strings.
focus: Dynamic contrast between powerful staccato beats 1 & 3 and light, softer beats 2 & 4
musicalRole: Classic orchestral tango guitar pulse, providing drive without cluttering low registers

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Marcato — Marcato 1–3 Pesante / Sin Staccato (Botto Ej. 8)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Marcato 1-3 variant from Mariano Botto (p. 25, Ej. 8). Beats 1 and 3 are sustained for their full quarter-note value with deep tenuto/pesante weight, creating an ominous, heavy tango march.
focus: Full sustained quarter-note weight on odd beats versus short staccato on even beats
musicalRole: Dramatic pesante accompaniment used in dramatic sections of tangos like La Cumparsita and Chiqué

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Tango — Acompañamiento en Dos con Negras / Staccato (Botto Ej. 12)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: En dos accompaniment using quarter notes on beats 1 and 3 followed by quarter rests (p. 26, Ej. 12). Gives the space and rhythmic breathing of traditional 2/4 tango pulse.
focus: Clean space on beats 2 and 4, creating the open 2-beat tango feel
musicalRole: Traditional rhythmic foundation supporting singer or solo bandoneón

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Tango — Acompañamiento Combinado en Dos y Cuatro (Botto Ej. 13)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Arrangement combining en dos (half notes) with en cuatro (quarter notes) from Mariano Botto (p. 27, Ej. 13). Shifts dynamically between open sustained harmony and driving rhythmic pulse.
focus: Smooth dynamic shift between sustained half-note chords and four-beat marcato
musicalRole: Dynamic pacing in tango guitar arrangements

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Tango — La Síncopa Clásica de Tango (Botto Ej. 15)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: The defining syncopation of Argentine Tango from Mariano Botto (p. 28, Ej. 15). An eighth-note attack on beat 1 is followed by a heavily accented dotted-quarter on the upbeat ("and" of 1), resolving to a deep bass on beat 3.
focus: Off-beat chord accentuation and staccato choke on beat 1-and
musicalRole: The rhythmic engine and propulsion of modern and golden age tango

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Síncopa Anticipada — Tres Variantes (Botto Ej. 16)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Three anticipation methods for the tango síncopa from Mariano Botto (p. 28, Ej. 16). Bar 1 anticipations with two 16th-notes; Bar 2 anticipations with an eighth-note; Bar 3 full melodic run into the syncopated chord.
focus: Mastering micro-anticipations before landing on the syncopated off-beat chord
musicalRole: Bandoneón-style guitar articulation introducing rhythmic variety into the phrase

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Tango — El Arrastre en la Síncopa (Botto Ej. 20)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Combining the arrastre with the syncopation from Mariano Botto (p. 30, Ej. 20). The slide enters into beat 1 without a right-hand pluck; the low strings ring solely from the sliding left hand, and the treble chord is struck hard on the upbeat.
focus: Unplucked left-hand slide onto beat 1 followed by an explosive staccato off-beat chord
musicalRole: High-intensity syncopation in classic orquestas typical of Troilo and Pugliese

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Tango — Melodía para Tango Clásico (Botto Ej. 21)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Complete classical tango melody from Mariano Botto (p. 31, Ej. 21). Written in A minor / A major with expressive turns, rubato cadences, and dramatic chromatic voice-leading.
focus: Cantabile guitar phrasing with subtle tempo fluctuations and tone coloration
musicalRole: Solo or lead concert tango guitar voice

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Tango — Acompañamiento con Bordonas en 2 y 4 (Botto Ej. 25)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Fourth accompaniment arrangement from Mariano Botto (p. 39, Ej. 25). Beats 2 and 4 are struck exclusively on the bass strings (bordonas) while beats 1 and 3 carry full chord punches.
focus: Low bass string thumb percussions on even beats contrasting with full mid-range chords
musicalRole: Traditional Argentine guitar accompaniment used by Roberto Grela and Ubaldo De Lío

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Tango Rítmico — Variación en Semicorcheas (Botto Ej. 26)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Fast sixteenth-note motoric variation from Mariano Botto (p. 41, Ej. 26). Echoes Roberto Grela’s guitar variations with continuous picking, sharp dynamic accents, and running scalar turns.
focus: Fast alternate picking on 16th-note tango variations (púa y contrapúa)
musicalRole: Virtuosic variation section (variación tanguera) showcasing technical agility

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Tango — Melodía de Tango Rítmico en Do Menor (Botto Ej. 27)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Dynamic rhythmic tango theme in C minor from Mariano Botto (p. 43, Ej. 27). Uses sharp staccato 8th-note attacks, triplet flourishes, and sudden syncopated stops.
focus: Crisp rhythmic execution with staccato stops and triplet turns
musicalRole: Up-tempo rhythmic tango lead theme (estilo D’Arienzo / Biagi)

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Vals — Acompañamiento Elaborado para Tango Rítmico (Botto Ej. 29)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Advanced rhythmic accompaniment from Mariano Botto (p. 46, Ej. 29). Features rapid syncopated chops, chromatic voice leading (G7 - Cm - D7/A - Ab7 - G7 - D° - C7 - C#7/G#), and walking basslines.
focus: Fast chord changes and chromatic bass counterpoint at high rhythmic tango tempo
musicalRole: Driving rhythm guitar supporting fast bandoneón variations

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Tango Canción — Intro Rubato y Acompañamiento (Botto Ej. 31)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Tango Canción arrangement from Mariano Botto (p. 50, Ej. 31). Begins with a contemplative rubato arpeggiated introduction in Am - Edim - D#dim - Em, then moves into a gentle, singing Emaj7 accompaniment.
focus: Rubato arpeggio phrasing and expressive chord-melody touch in lyrical tango style
musicalRole: Vocal accompaniment for classic tango lyrics (Gardel, Manzi, Discépolo)

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Vals Tango / Vals Criollo — Célula Rítmica en 3/4 (Botto Ej. 34)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Foundational Vals Tango rhythm in 3/4 from Mariano Botto (p. 54, Ej. 34). Beat 1 sounds the deep bass note, while Beats 2 and 3 carry staccato chords, with a pronounced, crisp accent on Beat 2.
focus: The characteristic Argentine vals pulse: heavy bass on 1, sharp accent on 2, light release on 3
musicalRole: Essential accompaniment for Argentine vals criollo (Desde el alma, Palomita blanca)

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Vals Tango — Variación con Bajo y Blanca Sostenida (Botto Ej. 35)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Vals variation from Mariano Botto (p. 55, Ej. 35). Alternates the standard 3-beat pulse with a measure where beat 1 is bass and beat 2 is a held half-note chord, creating a graceful swaying swing.
focus: Alternating active staccato vals bars with sustained two-beat chord holds
musicalRole: Creates dynamic breathing and elegant swaying in vals criollo accompaniments

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Milonga Campera — Célula Rítmica 3+3+2 (Botto Ej. 40)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Foundational rural milonga cell from Mariano Botto (p. 64, Ej. 40). Written in 2/4 meter with 8 sixteenth-notes grouped into [3 + 3 + 2] accents (dotted-eighth + dotted-eighth + eighth), forming the bedrock of Argentine folklore and tango.
focus: Mastery of the [3 + 3 + 2] syncopation across two beats in 2/4
musicalRole: Fundamental rhythmic DNA connecting rural gaucho song to urban milonga

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Milonga Campera — Patrón de Arpegios Tradicional (Botto Ej. 41)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Traditional fingerstyle arpeggio pattern for milonga campera from Mariano Botto (p. 65, Ej. 41). The thumb plays the alternating bass on beats 1 and 2, while fingers i-m-a articulate fluid arpeggios in Am - E7.
focus: Independent thumb bordoneo with continuous right-hand arpeggios (p-i-m-a)
musicalRole: Acoustic guitar accompaniment for payadores, Atahualpa Yupanqui, and milonga campera

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Milonga Porteña / Ciudadana — Célula Rítmica Bailable (Botto Ej. 52)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Crisp urban milonga rhythm from Mariano Botto (p. 69, Ej. 52). Fast 2/4 meter with dotted eighth + sixteenth + two eighths, driving the energetic footwork of Buenos Aires milonga dancers.
focus: Fast, crisp 2/4 staccato rhythm with dotted syncopation on beat 1
musicalRole: Dancefloor motor for urban milonga (Milonga sentimental, Milonga de mis amores)

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Milonga Porteña — Acompañamiento con Bordoneos (Botto Ej. 55)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Advanced milonga porteña accompaniment from Mariano Botto (p. 74, Ej. 55). Incorporates fast 16th-note running basslines (bordoneos) and chromatic chord substitutions (E7/G#, F7/C, Eb7/Bb, E7/B) answering the syncopated chord chops.
focus: Fast alternating bass bordoneos and sharp syncopated chord answers
musicalRole: Lead rhythm guitar in Argentine guitar quartet or milonga trio

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: Armonía Tanguera — Hacer Cantar al Bajo (Botto Ej. 60)
bookReference: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
description: Master harmony exercise from Mariano Botto (p. 83, Ej. 60). Shows how to make the bass sing ("hacer cantar al bajo") by connecting inverted triads, Maj7, m7, and diminished chords in a walking chromatic bassline over Cmaj7 - G7/D - C/E - Ebdim - Dm7 - A7/E - Dm/F - G7/B.
focus: Continuous melodic bass counterpoint connecting functional tango chord inversions
musicalRole: Sophisticated harmonic framework for arranging tangos for solo guitar or guitar duo

source.title: Cómo tocar tango en guitarra
source.author: Ramos, Ariel E. & Botto, Mariano

title: El Dominguero — Terceras con Pedal en Sol (Kvitko p. 27)
description: Estudio para púa Nº 1 from Diego "Dipi" Kvitko (p. 27). Develops downstroke pick attack consistency on harmonized thirds on the 2nd and 3rd strings while sounding a repeating open G pedal bass.
focus: Downstroke pick precision on harmonized diatonic thirds over open string drone
musicalRole: Plectrum technique study for Guardia Vieja and traditional tango guitar soloists

title: La Yumba — Efecto Yumbado de Osvaldo Pugliese (Graciano)
bookReference: Método de guitarra tango
description: The monumental Yumbado effect of Osvaldo Pugliese from Julián Graciano. Beats 1 and 3 feature a massive, low-register dragging chord (the "YUM") with heavy arrastre, followed by an ultra-short, choked staccato on beats 2 and 4 (the "BA").
focus: Visceral dynamic contrast between dragging heavy bass downbeats and razor-sharp choked upbeats
musicalRole: Signature Pugliese orchestral rhythm in tango guitar transcription

source.title: Método de guitarra tango
source.author: Julián Graciano

title: Tango — Doble Síncopa Tanguera (Graciano)
bookReference: Método de guitarra tango
description: Chained double syncopation from Julián Graciano. The off-beat accent on the upbeat of 1 ties across beat 2 into another syncopated punch on the upbeat of 3, creating modern metric suspension.
focus: Executing chained syncopated off-beat accents without losing the underlying meter
musicalRole: Modern and post-Piazzolla tango rhythmic framework

source.title: Método de guitarra tango
source.author: Julián Graciano

title: Tango Bass — Marcato en 4 con Choke (Arcella)
bookReference: Tango Bass
description: Authentic Tango double-bass and electric bass marcato from Bucky Arcella. All 4 quarter notes are articulated with deep low attack and choked immediately using left-hand string damping, creating the percussive backbone of the orquesta típica.
focus: Immediate left-hand finger release for clean, dry quarter-note staccato bass notes
musicalRole: Orchestral bass foundation locking with the bandoneón left-hand marcato

source.title: Tango Bass
source.author: Bucky Arcella

title: Tango Bass — Síncopa con Arrastre (Arcella)
bookReference: Tango Bass
description: Bass síncopa with arrastre from Bucky Arcella. The bass slides upward two semitones into the syncopated upbeat, landing with heavy percussive accent, followed by a dry low root on beat 3.
focus: Low-string glissando into syncopated upbeat accent with clean release
musicalRole: Propulsive rhythmic pivot propelling the entire tango ensemble forward

source.title: Tango Bass
source.author: Bucky Arcella

title: Libertango — Riff Rítmico de 3+3+2 en Guitarras (Diego Sola p. 19)
description: The iconic Astor Piazzolla 3+3+2 ostinato arranged for two guitars by Diego Sola (p. 19). Eight eighth-notes grouped into [3 + 3 + 2] accents over an Am chord with chromatic descending inner voice (A -> G# -> G -> F# -> F).
focus: Continuous [3 + 3 + 2] 8th-note ostinato with chromatic descending voice leading
musicalRole: Modern tango nuevo motor driving Piazzolla’s masterpiece

title: Semba — Semba Foundational Bassline (Angola)
description: The primary parent rhythm of Kizomba. Fast, playful, and percussive 2/4 (or fast 4/4) Angolan pulse featuring syncopated octave leaps, chromatic drop-ins, and strong upbeats that lock with dikanza (scraper) and congas.
focus: Playful syncopated octave bouncing and 16th-note pickups characteristic of Angolan Semba
musicalRole: Primary melodic bass foundation driving traditional Angolan Semba and live Kizomba bands

title: Semba — Kabetula & Kasukuta Carnival Bass (Luanda/Bengo)
description: Fast, aggressive carnival rhythm from Luanda and Bengo provinces. High-intensity syncopation and galloping 16th-note figures that drive carnival street dancers and influenced fast modern Kizomba variations.
focus: Fast, continuous 16th-note syncopated stamina and percussive ghost notes
musicalRole: Carnival street band bass driver locking with deep surdo and snare drums

title: Kilapanda Urban Groove — 1970s Electric Bass Fusion
description: 1970s Angolan urban fusion created by legendary Luanda electric bands (Os Jovens do Prenda, Kiezos). Translates traditional rural percussion into rolling melodic electric basslines, forming the direct bridge to modern Kizomba.
focus: Melodic lyrical bass counterpoint running through standard I - IV - V progressions
musicalRole: Pioneered the melodic, vocal role of electric bass in Lusophone African popular music

title: Congolese Rumba / Soukous — Sebene Interlocking Lead Guitar
description: The celebrated high-register guitar figures (sebene) of Congolese masters (Franco, Docteur Nico, Diblo Dibala) that profoundly shaped Caribbean Zouk (Kassav’) and early Kizomba guitar comping. Cyclical, shimmering 1-3-5 arpeggios.
focus: Clean, lightning-fast high-register arpeggio picking on the top three strings
musicalRole: Lead sebene guitar driving the peak dance climax in Congolese rumba and soukous

title: Congolese Rumba / Soukous — Rolling Melodic Bass
description: The rolling, syncopated basslines of Congolese Rumba that directly influenced Caribbean cadence and Antillean bassists in the 1970s and 80s. Melodic, bouncy root-third-fifth-octave runs that weave around the kick drum.
focus: Continuous syncopated bouncing across major triads with driving pulse
musicalRole: Harmonic and rhythmic foundation of Congolese popular music

title: Calypso — Cadence-Lypso Driving Bassline
description: Driving electric bass groove from classic 1970s Cadence-Lypso recordings. Fuses the swinging tumbao of Haitian compas with the driving calypso kick-drum syncopation.
focus: Propulsive off-beat syncopations with deep low-end punch
musicalRole: Rhythmic cornerstone bridging Haitian and Lesser Antilles dance traditions

title: Chouval Bwa — Tibwa Bamboo Pattern on Guitar (Martinique)
description: Traditional Martinican carousel rhythm (Chouval Bwa). The interlocking 16th-note bamboo stick (tibwa) pattern is adapted onto guitar muted single-note picking, establishing the high-speed rhythmic density that Pierre-Edouard Décimus synthesized into Zouk.
focus: Muted 16th-note rhythmic picking replicating the West Indian tibwa percussion stick
musicalRole: Traditional Antillean folk groove and foundational texture of modern Zouk

title: Zouk Béton — Slap & Pop Bass Groove (Kassav’ Style)
description: The explosive high-tech bass groove created by Georges Décimus and Kassav’ in 1984. Combines heavy 16th-note funk thumb-slaps, popping octaves, and syncopated Antillean carnival brass stops.
focus: Fast, aggressive slap and pop technique on high-energy Caribbean festival groove
musicalRole: Signature powerhouse bass style that turned Zouk into a worldwide stadium phenomenon

title: Zouk-Love — Arpeggiated Chorus Guitar Comping
description: Lush, sparkling electric guitar comping from late 80s / 90s Zouk-Love hits (Gilles Floro, Jean-Philippe Marthely). Uses wide stereo chorus, digital delay, and extended major 9th and minor 9th voicings.
focus: Extended chord arpeggiation with clean chorused tone floating over the tresillo beat
musicalRole: Harmonic atmosphere and romantic intimacy in Zouk-Love and Cabo-Zouk productions

title: Urban Kiz — 808 Half-Time Syncopation & Staccato Accents
description: Modern European dance style developed in Paris (Curtis Seldon, Enah Lebon) blending Kizomba footwork with R&B, hip-hop, and pop. Features electronic 808 sub-bass drops, sudden syncopated stops, and linear staccato accents.
focus: Sudden stop-and-go syncopations, 808 pitch slides, and crisp staccato cuts
musicalRole: Modern urban electronic bassline supporting stop-and-go choreography

focus: Bass New Orleans: Root–Fifth–Sixth Groove
